10/10 – The Assassin’s Creed We’ve Been Waiting For

Assassin’s Creed Shadows is everything I hoped it would be and more. From the moment the game starts, it pulls you into a breathtaking vision of feudal Japan. The world is alive—villages bustle with activity, forests feel dangerous and mysterious, and every rooftop is an opportunity for stealth.

Combat feels fluid and weighty. Switching between the samurai’s brutal precision and the shinobi’s shadowy finesse creates endless gameplay variety. Stealth is finally back at the heart of the series, with tools and mechanics that reward patience, creativity, and timing. At the same time, the open fights are cinematic and satisfying, making you feel like you’re living out a Kurosawa film.

The story is gripping, grounded in Japanese history while weaving in the rich Assassin’s Creed lore we know and love. The characters are memorable, the choices feel meaningful, and the atmosphere is unmatched.

Visually, the game is stunning—sunsets over temples, rain-slick rooftops, snow falling on battlefields. Every frame could be a screenshot-worthy moment. The soundtrack ties it all together with a mix of tense stealth pieces and sweeping, emotional scores.

Ubisoft has finally struck the perfect balance between classic Assassin’s Creed gameplay and modern RPG depth. This is the pinnacle of the series, and one of the best open-world experiences I’ve ever played.

If you’re a fan of Assassin’s Creed, samurai, or just incredible video games in general, this is an absolute must-play.

10/10 – A masterpiece in every sense.

This isn't a bad game, but it's probably the worst executed AC game that I've ever played. Bad controller integration, audio drop outs requiring PC restart. Many, many areas where half of the enemies can be found inexplicably asleep face-down on the ground outside in the middle of the day. 'Recommended' gameplay settings with no obvious purpose other than to increase play time by padding out your experience wandering around looking for something stupid for no good reason. Don't bother replaying an entire castle twice because one of the two PCs isn't strong enough to push a single box three feet and find a hand fan.

Historical nitpick - the main plot covers a historical period of two weeks but the game stretches it out into years and years for no reason other than to cram in bloat. Very apt, actually. I changed my mind, it is bad.

Most people will criticize my opinion or paint me as a surface level racist. Frankly, I don’t give a damn about any of that. The game is absolutely worse off for the forced inclusion of a second protagonist, period.

The developers were smoking crack when they green lit this decision.

Go play Ghost of Tsushima or Yotei instead.

I know I'm going to sink over 50 hours into this, but mostly because it's so bloated with repetitive side quests that seem almost unavoidable. Like why do I have to do what feels like hundreds of pointless quicktime events just to level up a skill tree?????
It's also very clunky during 'main' cutscenes, even on a decent machine. The worst part about them though is how they break the 'immersion mode', because these major cutscenes are clearly animated for the English voices only.

That aside, it is pretty and I enjoy being able to play as both characters (even if I do spend 90% of the time as Naoe). The combat is also fun but can become a slog quickly. Being able to fully customise the base is also nice.

Assassin's Creed Shadows should have been better. I began playing Shadows at the launch of the game, I had been running through all the games in preparation for this release. I played for roughly 30ish hours, then got distracted and moved to a different game. Coming back in December '25 to finish the game I came to realize why I stepped away for a period. The game is bland, the gameplay is repetitive, the story is boring, the characters are poorly written, and there isn't anything to push the story of AC forward. I loved the world, I loved the movement, I loved having a new "AC" game. I want to be able to recommend it to more than just the most dedicated fans of the series, but I can't. I am sad to say I do not recommend Shadows.
